items.stem: A Claude-generated test passes even after you deliberately break the function it covers. What does this indicate?

options.text: The test is not actually exercising the behaviour and must be fixed
options.rationale: Correct: a test that passes against broken code provides no protection.

options.text: The function is correct after all
options.rationale: The function is broken by design; the test simply fails to catch it.

options.text: The test is extra strict and can be trusted
options.rationale: It is not strict; it is ineffective.

options.text: CI should be configured to skip the test
options.rationale: Skipping a useless test removes even the appearance of coverage without fixing it.

items.explanation: Correct: a test that passes against broken code provides no protection.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions should block a merge to the protected branch? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A required test check is failing
options.rationale: Correct: merging over red tests ships known-broken code.

options.text: Required review has not been completed
options.rationale: Correct: unreviewed changes bypass a key quality control.

options.text: The branch name does not match a naming convention
options.rationale: Naming style is cosmetic and should not block a sound change.

options.text: The pull request has fewer than ten commits
options.rationale: Commit count is not a quality signal.

items.explanation: Correct: merging over red tests ships known-broken code.

items.stem: What is the correct way to use a deployment secret in a GitHub Actions job?

options.text: Inject it from a secret store and keep it out of logs
options.rationale: Correct: secrets must be injected securely and never printed.

options.text: Echo it during the job to confirm it is set
options.rationale: Echoing a secret leaks it into the build log.

options.text: Hard-code it in the workflow file
options.rationale: Committing a secret exposes it in the repository history.

options.text: Store it in a plaintext file in the repo
options.rationale: A plaintext secret in the repo is a credential leak.

items.explanation: Correct: secrets must be injected securely and never printed.
